page.layout: One printed page (left page of an opening) with a main text column in the centre; a narrow strip of text at the right edge belonging to the facing page, partly cut off, with marginal notes on the right side of the text column. Running head at top; page number at top left. Text column ends with a catchword-like "Officium" set at the right below the last line.

p.i: Subditi agnoscant in Principe suo non tantum ius maiestatis Politicum, sed etiam Ecclesiasticum, atq; adeò præstent ei obedientiam in omnibus quæ ex verbo Dei ad cultum & salutem animarum Princeps constituit.

main_text.p: Subditi in specie consyderati, sunt personæ Ecclesiasticæ, de quib. Canon est:

p.i: Ministri Ecclesiarum & alie personæ religiosæ agnoscant in Principe ius maiestatis Ecclesiasticæ, neq; peregrinam Iurisdictionem quærant.

main_text.p: Nempe ipse Christus & Apostoli iurisdictionem Rom. Imper. agnouerūt, & fuit 1, Christus ciuis in Capernaum, quæ vrbs tum Romano imperio subiecta erat, 2, soluit etiam vectigal iis, qui id in Iudæa nomine Imperatoris exigebant. 3, agnouit etiam iudicium præsidis Rom. & coram illo sponte ultrò stetit. Et sane valde absurdum est, velle sub patrocinio & sub defensione Magistratus viuere, & commodis omnibus frui vna cum reliquis subditis, & interim nolle agnoscere potestatem & iurisdictionem Principis, à quo omnia ista habes: Quod notetur contra ius Canonicum, & contra omnes Pontificios, qui personas Ecclesiasticas eximunt à Iurisdictione Politici Magistratus, & Romæ etiam sc. iudicari voluntii, qui 500 miliarib. Roma abfunt. Ex his a facile determinabitur quæstio, vtrū Sacerdotes sint pars Reip. de qua quæst. tum alii multi, tum Hofius disputat in lib. de Monarch. Eccles. pag. 91. Nam si id certum est, vt certū est, personas Ecclesiasticas subiectas esse iurisdictioni Principis, sequitur et eas esse Reip. capiti subiectas & legib. Reip. obnoxias.

page.notes: The right-hand strip is a fragment of the facing page, cut off and largely illegible; its text is not transcribed. Marginal notes on the left margin of the text column are absent; the printed side notes at the right of the column are mostly cut off by the binding and not legible. Some words in the main column are doubtful, notably "Chrift" with superscript, "Hofius", and the numbers in the text; "Officium" at the foot may be a catchword.
